title: Quant Runtime Integration Playbook — INT8/AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 (draft)
content:
Overview:

This playbook captures an implementation-minded integration plan for supporting multiple low-precision execution formats (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) inside the serving runtime. Goal is to define the runtime decisions, kernel compatibility constraints, KV cache implications, scheduling and fallback behavior necessary for safe, high-performance rollout across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: runtime engineers, kernel integrators, SREs responsible for model rollouts.
- Scope: per-op kernel selection, memory layout/packing constraints, KV cache storage/transfer semantics, batching behavior, fallback and testing expectations. Not covering model quantization training procedures.

Design goals and non-goals:
- Goals: predictable latency, minimal correctness regressions, graceful fallbacks when incompatible kernels/memory are encountered, measurable telemetry for degradations.
- Non-goals: automatic model re-quantization inside the runtime; heavy-weight per-request calibration.

Key concepts and terms (short):
- weight-format: GPTQ/AWQ/int8-fp32-scale/fp8-e4m3, represents how model weights are stored on disk and in memory.
- op-kernel: an implementation of an operator (matmul, attention, rmsnorm) optimized for a target precision.
- quantized-exec-path: an execution graph where a subset or all kernels run in low-precision using specialized kernels.
- mixed-precision fallback: runtime decision to run an op in higher precision if constraints not met.

High-level strategy:
1) At model load time, inspect model metadata (weight-format, per-layer quant params). Build a candidate execution plan: map ops to specialized kernels where available and compatible.
2) Validate compatibility of kernel chain and shared buffers (KV cache layout, attention scratch buffers). If any constraint fails, mark op for fallback.
3) Emit a compact runtime plan with flags per-route: quantized=true/false, quant-format=AWQ/GPTQ/INT8/FP8, fallback-policy=can-fallback|no-fallback.
4) At request-time, use the plan and lightweight heuristics (sequence length, batch size) to decide whether to route to quantized device pool or float pool.

Kernel compatibility checklist (what a kernel integration must declare):
- supported weight formats (list): e.g. [gptq, awq, int8-symmetric, fp8-e4m3].
- input type(s): packed-int8, packed-fp8, float32 (for dequantized path).
- required buffer alignment: 64B/128B and specific stride rules for packed weight layout.
- per-op temporary scratch size upper bound (bytes) and whether it uses device-local memory only.
- kv-cache compatibility: can consume/produce quantized KV blocks? (yes/no) and required KV layout.
- deterministic: whether kernel introduces non-determinism.
- supported max-seqlen and block-size constraints.

Memory layout and packing rules (summary):
- We require explicit metadata describing per-layer packing: vector-length, tile-size (e.g., 32x128 row-major tiles), scale-storage location (inline vs side-table), and channel-order (OC-major vs IC-major).
- For GPTQ/AWQ, metadata must include per-channel scales and quant-block shape. Runtime must be able to map weight indices -> physical offset without re-packing.
- KV cache: when kernels support quantized KV, cache blocks are stored as (value_qbytes, scale_bytes) with alignment matching kernel requirements. When kernels only accept dequantized KV, runtime must support lazy dequantization into a reuse buffer.

KV cache semantics and migration patterns:
- Two canonical KV formats in our runtime: QUANT_KV and FLOAT_KV.
- Model load registers its preferred_kv_format; per-request runtime plan indicates whether cache should be populated in QUANT_KV.
- Migration rule: if an incoming request with QUANT_KV cache size S touches a layer that only supports FLOAT_KV, convert the minimal subset needed (per layer, per beam) to FLOAT_KV lazily on first use.
- Eviction: QUANT_KV entries are cheaper (packed) so eviction thresholds differ. Eviction and eviction metrics must be emitted separately (kv_eviction_quant, kv_eviction_float).
- Checkpoint/serialization: prefer storing the canonical on-disk form in the model bundle (weights), not the runtime cache. For stateful long-lived sessions, provide operator to export flattened FLOAT_KV for debugging.

Scheduling and batching behavior with quantized kernels:
- Quantized kernels generally achieve higher throughput but sometimes slightly higher tail latency due to packing/unpacking. Scheduler policy suggestions:
  * prefer quantized pool for large-batch, throughput-first routes (e.g., embeddings, batch-generation offline).
  * prefer float pool or mixed path for latency-sensitive short sequences when dequantization overhead may dominate.
- Continuous batching: when accumulating a batch, prefer to group requests by quant-format and weight-format to avoid per-batch kernel reconfiguration. The batching window should respect a format-homogeneity threshold: e.g., only batch together requests with identical quant-format AND identical sequence-length bucket.

Fallback and graceful degradation policy:
- Fallback triggers: missing kernel for op, incompatible KV layout, insufficient scratch memory, or observed correctness regression (model-eval metric drop beyond threshold).
- Policy options:
  * soft-fallback: auto-fallback single op to float kernel at the cost of extra dequantization and memory; keep serving.
  * hard-fallback: abort quantized plan and route request to float pool (used when multiple ops incompatible or per-request SLO requires strict correctness).
- Runtime should prefer soft-fallback for single-op incompatibilities as first-line; hard-fallback reserved for cross-layer incompatibilities or when soft-fallback’s extra latency would violate tail SLO.

Attention-specific constraints and notes:
- Softmax numerical stability: FP8/INT8 attention logits need bias-safety checks. Kernels must provide an intermediate accumulator (FP32) or safe range checks; otherwise declare "requires-dequantize-before-softmax".
- Rotary/ALiBi and position-encoding: some quant formats lose small-scale positional signals; document per-kernel whether positional multipliers should be fused pre-quantization or applied in float.
- KV partitioning: attention KV blocks are often split into fixed-size shards. Quantized KV shards should preserve shard boundaries to avoid cross-block dequantization costs.

Dequantization strategies (practical patterns):
- eager-dequantize: convert entire weight or KV block to float at load time. Simple but memory-heavy; used for small models or when many kernels lack quant support.
- lazy-dequantize: dequantize only the requested tile/row on first use and cache the dequantized tile in ephemeral buffer. Balance memory vs CPU/GPU time.
- on-the-fly fused-dequant: kernels that accept packed weights and perform dequant inside the matmul (preferred for throughput).
Runtime should pick strategy per-layer based on kernel declarations and per-route memory budget.

Operator flags and bundle metadata (recommended keys):
- quant_support: "none|partial|full"
- weight_format: "fp32|int8|gptq|awq|fp8-e4m3"
- kv_format_supported: "quant|float|both"
- pack_tile: "rXcY" (tile descriptor)
- dequant_behavior: "eager|lazy|kernel-fused"
- fallback_policy: "soft|hard|deny"

Diagnostics, telemetry and rollout signals:
- Emit per-request plan decisions: chosen_plan_id, used_quant_pool, fallback_reason (if any).
- Quant-specific metrics: quant_cache_hit_ratio, quant_patch_dequant_count, quant_fallback_rate, quant_latency_p99_delta.
- Quality signals: tie model-eval prompts to rollout groups; alert if generation quality drop > X% after quantized rollout.

Testing checklist for kernel integrators (before rolling to prod):
- Unit correctness: per-op numeric comparators against fp32 baseline on representative tensors (max abs, relative error, and argmax consistency).
- Integration smoke: load model, run short generation with 1..8 tokens, compare token-by-token diffs under tolerance.
- KV roundtrip: populate, evict, and restore cache in quant format and validate identical semantics to float path within tolerance.
- Stress tests: variable sequence lengths, batch compositions, concurrent requests to ensure no cross-request corruption of shared buffers.
- Memory and scratch budgets: verify reported scratch usage under peak batch and sequence length.
- Telemetry: synthetic rollout with Canary traffic that emits quant_fallback_rate and quality metrics.

Performance targets (informational baseline):
- Small LLMs (~1–3B): single-stream latency p50 within 1.1x of float for fuse-dequant kernels; throughput improvement 2x–4x on A100.
- Medium LLMs (~7–20B): expected throughput increase 1.5x–3x, p99 latency may increase slightly depending on lazy dequantization.
- Note: H100 may require different kernel tiling—kernel metadata MUST declare tested device families.

Runtime pseudocode for plan selection (conceptual):

  on_model_load(bundle):
    for layer in bundle.layers:
      read weight_format, pack_meta, kernel_caps
      if kernel_caps.supports(weight_format):
        assign op->quant_kernel
      else if kernel_caps.can_run_dequantized:
        mark op->soft_fallback_dequant
      else
        mark op->hard_fallback_to_float
    produce plan

  on_request(plan, seq_len, route_flags):
    if plan.has_hard_fallback and route_flags.strict_correctness:
      route_to_float_pool()
    else if seq_len < threshold and plan.mix_dequant_overhead_high:
      maybe_route_to_float_pool()
    else
      execute_using_plan()

Open issues and decisions needed:
- Standardize a minimal pack metadata schema (JSON/BLOB) that fits in model bundle without inflating download size.
- Decide an SLO for acceptable fallback rate in staged rollout (e.g., <0.5% soft-fallback in canary).
- Precise definition of "quality regression" metric we use to auto-roll back quantized routes.

Rollout plan (recommended):
1) Internal canary with synthetic traffic and strict telemetry for 1–2 weeks.
2) Beta traffic with small percentage of customers with opt-in, monitor quality and fallback metrics.
3) Gradual ramp with automated rollback if quant_fallback_rate or generation-quality drops exceed thresholds.

Appendix: quick integration notes for kernel authors:
- Always provide a compact capability manifest alongside kernel binary. It must include supported weight formats, device families and maximal sequence length.
- Avoid implicit padding assumptions; declare required alignment explicitly.
- If your kernel can accept quantized KV, provide a small helper that converts the model bundle KV packing metadata to the kernel’s expected offsets.

Contact and maintenance:
- Owner: David Kim (eng-serving-runtime)
- For kernel onboarding or device-specific issues, contact Priya Narang (applied-ml).

This document is intentionally pragmatic — feel free to propose additions to the compatibility matrix or new telemetry fields. Next steps: finalize pack-metadata schema and produce a short conformance test harness to validate kernel manifests.
